- What the Fed did: Held the federal funds rate at 5.25–5.50% and kept balance sheet run-off at established caps ($60B Treasuries, $35B agency MBS). Implementation rates unchanged (IORB 5.4%, ON RRP 5.3%); standing facilities in place to support transmission.
- Macro tone: Describes growth as solid, job gains strong, unemployment low, and inflation easing—but still elevated. Risks to goals seen as moving into better balance; no cuts until greater confidence inflation is heading sustainably to 2%.
- SLOOS overlay (credit supply and demand): Banks report tight credit conditions that temper the upbeat macro tone.
  • C&I: Large banks report weaker demand; standards remain tight.  
  • CRE: Broad tightening of standards across construction, multifamily, and nonfarm nonresidential; foreign banks also report tighter CRE standards.  
  • Households: Auto loan standards tightened; for mortgages, standards unchanged for GSE-eligible but tighter for non-QM/jumbo segments.
- Implications: Persistent credit tightening and weaker loan demand suggest restrictive financial conditions are still biting, reinforcing the Fed’s cautious “no cuts until confidence” guidance and arguing for a restrained read on the outlook despite solid current activity.

Overall take: Constructively toned on growth and risk balance, but SLOOS-confirmed credit headwinds warrant a more cautious sentiment than the statement alone.
